hook.line: You want to nudge someone without giving an order. Spanish has a soft way to say "it would be good if…" and "what if…", and it works on friends, family and business partners alike.
hook.es: Estaría bien que vinieras a la audiencia.
hook.en: It would be good if you came to the hearing. (to a friend)

examples.es: Estaría bien que saliéramos un día con Vale.
examples.en: It would be nice if we went out with Vale some day.

examples.es: ¿Y si fuéramos este año a la costa?
examples.en: What if we went to the coast this year?

examples.es: No estaría mal que llamaras a tu abuela.
examples.en: It wouldn't be a bad idea for you to call your grandmother. (to a friend)

examples.es: Estaría bien que Tomás hablara con el dueño.
examples.en: It would be good if Tomás spoke to the owner.

examples.es: ¿Y si abriéramos más temprano los sábados?
examples.en: What if we opened earlier on Saturdays?

examples.es: No estaría mal que cambiáramos el menú.
examples.en: It wouldn't be a bad idea for us to change the menu.

rule:
To suggest something gently, start with *Estaría bien que* ("it would be good if") and put the next verb in the *-ra* form: *saliéramos*, *llamaras*, *hablara*. English does the same thing with "if we went".

*No estaría mal que* means almost the same, and sounds a little more modest.

For a quick "what if", use *¿Y si…?* with the same *-ra* form.

Here the *-ra* form is not about the past. It just turns an order into a possibility. If nobody in particular acts, skip *que*: *Estaría bien salir*.
smallPrint: Teachers call the *-ra* form the imperfect subjunctive, and *estaría* the conditional of *estar*.

readAndPick.es: Estaría bien que saliéramos un día con Vale.
options: It was nice that we went out with Vale.
It would be nice if we went out with Vale some day.
It is nice that we go out with Vale.

readAndPick.es: ¿Y si fuéramos este año a la costa?
options: What if we went to the coast this year?
Did we go to the coast this year?
We should have gone to the coast this year.

readAndPick.es: No estaría mal que llamaras a tu abuela.
options: It would be a bad idea for you to call your grandmother.
You didn't call your grandmother, and that's bad.
It wouldn't be a bad idea for you to call your grandmother.

readAndPick.es: Estaría bien que Tomás hablara con el dueño.
options: It would be good if Tomás spoke to the owner.
Tomás speaks to the owner, which is good.
It was good that Tomás spoke to the owner.

readAndPick.es: ¿Y si abriéramos más temprano los sábados?
options: We opened earlier on Saturdays.
What if we opened earlier on Saturdays?

readAndPick.es: No estaría mal que cambiáramos el menú.
options: It would be a bad idea for us to change the menu.
It wouldn't be a bad idea for us to change the menu.
We didn't change the menu, and that's not bad.

readAndPick.es: Estaría bien que vinieras a la audiencia.
options: It would be good if I came to the hearing.
It would be good if they came to the hearing.
It would be good if you came to the hearing. (to a friend)

readAndPick.es: Estaría bien que me ayudaras con las cuentas.
options: It would be good if I helped you with the accounts.
It would be good if you helped me with the accounts. (to a friend)
It would be good if she helped me with the accounts.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick the right form and type the whole sentence: *Estaría bien que ___ un día con Vale.* (*saliéramos* or *salimos*)
yourTurn.answer: Estaría bien que saliéramos un día con Vale.
yourTurn.why: After *estaría bien que*, the verb takes the *-ra* form: *saliéramos*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: What if we went to the coast this year?
yourTurn.answer: ¿Y si fuéramos este año a la costa?
accept: ¿Y si fuéramos a la costa este año?

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: It wouldn't be a bad idea for you to call your grandmother.
yourTurn.answer: No estaría mal que llamaras a tu abuela.
yourTurn.why: *No estaría mal que* plus the *-ra* form: *llamaras* is the *tú* version.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It would be good if Tomás spoke to the owner.
yourTurn.answer: Estaría bien que Tomás hablara con el dueño.
accept: Estaría bien que hablara Tomás con el dueño.
yourTurn.why: Someone else acts, so *que* and the *-ra* form: *hablara*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it a "what if" question: *Abrimos más temprano los sábados.* Say: What if we opened earlier on Saturdays?
yourTurn.answer: ¿Y si abriéramos más temprano los sábados?
yourTurn.why: Start with *¿Y si…?* and switch *abrimos* to *abriéramos*.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn it around: *Estaría bien que cambiáramos el menú.* Say: It wouldn't be a bad idea for us to change the menu.
yourTurn.answer: No estaría mal que cambiáramos el menú.
yourTurn.why: Swap *estaría bien* for *no estaría mal*; the *-ra* verb stays.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: It would be good if you came to the hearing.
yourTurn.answer: Estaría bien que vinieras a la audiencia.

pitfalls.wrong: Estaría bien que salimos un día con Vale.
pitfalls.right: Estaría bien que saliéramos un día con Vale.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *estaría bien que* the next verb takes the *-ra* form, like English "if we went".

pitfalls.wrong: Estaría bien de que saliéramos un día con Vale.
pitfalls.right: Estaría bien que saliéramos un día con Vale.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Que* comes straight after *bien*; there is no *de* in between.

pitfalls.wrong: Sería bien que saliéramos un día con Vale.
pitfalls.right: Estaría bien que saliéramos un día con Vale.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The set phrase uses *estar*: *estaría bien*, not *sería bien*.

personal: Suggest something gentle to a friend or someone at home, starting with *Estaría bien que…* and an *-ra* verb.
